'''Master of the Order''' was a title used to denote the elected leader of the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]]; during the last decades of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]] and was also used; by the [[New Jedi Order]]. Even though the title was separate from the title of [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]], the positions were oftentimes granted to the same individual.

==History==
Master of the Order was a title which had existed within the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] for much of its history, representing the elected leader of the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]]. Appointment of this position was reserved to the High Council's sitting members, with a unanimous vote needed to name a new leader. While not always the case, the Jedi Grand Master was frequently named leader of the High Council.<ref name="TJP" />

While many [[Jedi Master/Legends|Masters]] have held the title over the history of the Jedi, only a few names are remembered by historians. The earliest named Master of the Order was the [[Jenet/Legends|Jenet]] Grand Master [[Fae Coven]], who was appointed head of the Council and held the position for several centuries, meeting her future successor, [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]], before her death.<ref name="TJP" />

Master [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] held the title during the last years of the [[Golden Age of the Old Republic|Republic's Golden Age]], stepping down after the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle of Geonosis]] so as to take a more active role in the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. Grand Master [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] took up the title in Windu's absence, as he remained on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] to serve as [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] chief military adviser.<ref name="TCSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> At the end of the war, Chancellor Palpatine revealed himself as a [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] and ordered the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|disbanding]] of the Order. With the High Council dissolved and Master Yoda in exile, the term fell out of use for several decades.<ref name="ROTS" />

Before his death, the exiled Master Yoda helped [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] complete his [[Jedi training/Legends|training]] as a Jedi; Skywalker would eventually [[New Jedi Order|rebuild]] the Order, yet he did not form a Council until several years later.<ref name="The Swarm War">''[[Dark Nest III: The Swarm War]]''</ref> Leading the Order he built for many years, Skywalker was held responsible for the [[Second Galactic Civil War|actions]] of the Jedi-turned-Sith [[Darth Caedus|Jacen Solo]] by the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] government. After trying the Grand Master, [[Chief of State (Galactic Alliance)|Chief of State]] [[Natasi Daala]] [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exiled]] Skywalker from [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] and the Jedi Order in [[43 ABY|43.5 ABY]] until he could prove what had caused Solo's turn to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]. In the mean time, Skywalker and Daala agreed to the appointment of Master [[Kenth Hamner]] as acting Grand Master and leader of the Council, until Skywalker's return or the High Council elected another Master.<ref name="Omen" /><ref name="Outcast">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Outcast]]''</ref>

When tensions between Daala's Galactic Alliance and the Jedi Order grew, the Jedi refused to continue appeasing her demands of the Order. The Masters wanted to launch a wing of [[StealthX]]s to help Skywalker fight a new Sith [[Lost Tribe of Sith|threat]], but Hamner feared that the Galactic Alliance would think the launch was against them and would open fire on the StealthXs. However, when the Council discovered that Hamner had taken unilateral actions in making an agreement with Alliance [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Nek Bwua'tu]] to stall the launch until Bwua'tu gave him permission, they removed him from his position as acting Grand Master and decided to launch the StealthXs. Hamner attempted to stop the StealthX launch, and in the ensuing [[Skirmish in the Operations Hangar|skirmish]] with Master [[Saba Sebatyne|Sebatyne]], he fell to his [[Death/Legends|death]]. The Masters then unanimously voted for Sebatyne, who had led the vote of no confidence against Hamner, as the new acting leader of the Jedi. She felt that the appointment was wrong, as she was deeply upset over her failure to prevent Hamner's death, but eventually accepted her position.<ref name="Vortex">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Vortex]]''</ref> Luke eventually returned to Coruscant and resumed his duty as leader of the Jedi.<ref name="Ascension">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Ascension]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The title "Master of the Order" first appeared in ''[[Yoda: Dark Rendezvous]]'', with Yoda being referred to as both "Grand Master of the Jedi Order" (another title introduced in the novel) and "Master of the Order," implying that the two titles were interchangeable. However, ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' later established that Master of the Order was a separate position from Grand Master, and that the position was normally held by Mace Windu, with Yoda only temporarily assuming the role when Windu was off-world.

Jedi Master [[Kol Skywalker]] was also described as being the leader of the Jedi Council in ''[[Star Wars: Legacy (2006) 0½|Star Wars: Legacy 0½]]''; this would seem to imply that he also held the title of Master of the Order. Also his brother, Bantha Rawk, referred to the Jedi High Council as "Kol's Council", which would also support this.<ref name="Legacy 25">[[Legacy (2006) 25|''Legacy'' (2006) 25]]</ref>
